meta.title: Why we hurt the people we need the most

Joseph Wright of Derby figures around firelight painting
plates.want: Wright of Derby, warmth and shadow (PD)

beats.text: On a freezing night, a huddle of hedgehogs press together to keep warm.
But the closer they move, the more their spines stab one another, and they spring apart.
Cold drives them back together. Pain drives them back apart. Back and forth, all night.
Schopenhauer said this is us. We need each other for warmth — and wound each other up close.
So we learn a middle distance: close enough to feel the heat, far enough to spare the spines.
He called that distance politeness and good manners — the compromise lonely creatures settle on.
The one who carries the most inner warmth needs the huddle least — and hurts no one.

source_note: Parable from Parerga and Paralipomena (public-domain translation) — paraphrased.
